chunks: Ibn Muskān from ʿUmar ibn al-Barāʾ said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to pray two rakʿahs as a fard (obligatory) prayer at the Maqām Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) until he arrived at Minā. He said, 'He prays them at Minā.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, a title for Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ لِلْفَرِيضَةِ: Two obligatory rakʿahs, referring specifically to the two units of prayer performed during the Hajj pilgrimage.
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Maqām Ibrāhīm (the Station of Abraham), a specific site in the Grand Mosque in Mecca associated with the Hajj rituals.
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, a plain and sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims spend the days of Tashrīq.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets the two rak'ahs of Hajj prayer at Maqam Ibrahim?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the principle of ease (yusr) in Hajj rituals, allowing the pilgrim to defer the missed obligatory prayer to Minā rather than disrupting the pilgrimage flow by returning to Mecca. It highlights the practical flexibility granted by the Ahl al-Bayt in balancing ritual completeness with the logistical realities of the Hajj journey. This specific location, Maqām Ibrāhīm, is traditionally viewed as a spiritual anchor where the pilgrim connects with the legacy of Prophet Ibrahim (AS).
